neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case is that three accused approached the house of Raja Singh. One of them fired at Baggar Singh, hitting him on the right thigh, causing him to fall. The accused then took Hoshiar Singh, another individual, away towards a village. Approximately 20 minutes later, the sound of three or four gunshots was heard. The next morning, the dead body of Hoshiar Singh was found. The post mortem report indicated that the deceased had only lacerated wounds, with no gunshot wounds present. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 307 IPC, while the High Court convicted them under Section 302 IPC. However, the Supreme Court found that the prosecution's case regarding the charge under Section 302 IPC was uncertain due to the absence of gunshot wounds on the deceased's body, leading to the acquittal of the accused on that charge.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that Hoshiar Singh was taken away by the accused and after 15/20 minutes gun shots were heard, leading to his death. They sought conviction under Section 302 IPC.

quotes.text: The prosecution case is that on 24.4.92 at about 8.30 p.m., the 3 accused came to the house of Raja Singh. Later, one of them fired at Baggar Singh on his right thigh. Baggar Singh fell down. Then the accused took away the deceased Hoshiar Singh towards village Heerawala. After about 20 minutes the sound of 3 or 4 shots was heard. Next morning the dead body of Hoshiar Singh was found.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the post mortem report showed only lacerated wounds on the dead body of Hoshiar Singh, with no gun shot wound, creating doubt about the charge under Section 302 IPC.

quotes.text: As per the post mortem report, there were only lacerated wounds on the dead body of the second victim - There was no gun shot wound on his body - Accused entitled to benefit of doubt and consequently acquitted of charge u/s.302

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle of the benefit of doubt to the accused in the absence of conclusive evidence of the charge under Section 302 IPC.

quotes.text: Accused entitled to benefit of doubt and consequently acquitted of charge u/s.302

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the appellants were found guilty under Section 325 IPC read with Section 34 IPC for firing a gunshot at Baggar Singh which hit him in the leg.

quotes.text: However, we are of the opinion that the appellants are guilty under Section 325 IPC read with Section 34 IPC because admittedly a gun shot was fired at Baggar Singh which hit him in the leg.

other_sentence_order.value: The court ordered that the sentence of imprisonment imposed on the appellants shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal, provided each of them furnishes personal bond in the sum of Rs. 20,000/- with two sureties in the sum of Rs. 10,000/- each to the satisfaction of the trial court. Their bonds are discharged accordingly.
